# Amanat

> Verified weather and storm-risk readings a contract can act on. A Telegraph Protocol miner, a scoring module, and a parametric cover contract on Base Sepolia.

Every answer is a weather report plus the scalars behind it: temperature, wind, gusts, precipitation, sea state, the nearest named cyclone, and a storm risk in [0,1] with the payout trigger at 0.75. The risk comes with an ensemble band (ECMWF, 51 members) and an Ed25519 attestation over the fields a contract settles on.

## Call it

- POST https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/forecast with `{"question": "Storm risk for Cebu in the next 6 hours?"}` or `{"lat": 10.32, "lon": 123.89, "hours": 6}`
- GET  https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/api/route?from=Cebu&to=Manila&speed=37 — risk along a route, each leg at the hour the vehicle reaches it
- GET  https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/api/backtest?lat=10.32&lon=123.89&start=2021-12-15&end=2021-12-18 — would the trigger have fired? Typhoon Rai, Cebu: yes, 1.000 at 13:00 UTC on 16 December
- GET  https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/api/jobable — which intents an on-chain ERC-8183 job cannot survive, and who on each one can receive one. every intent whose leader can be audited is closed; the rest have leaders whose registration YAML is published at 127.0.0.1 and cannot be checked.
- Paid, routed by the network: ask the Telegraph Engine for WEATHER_FORECAST, WEATHER_CHECK or STORM_ALERT over x402, $0.01

## Read it

- [Four ways in](https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/use): plain HTTP, MCP, the Engine, or an on-chain job — cheapest first
- [OpenAPI](https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/openapi.json): every route and schema
- [Signing key](https://amanat-miner.vercel.app/.well-known/amanat.json): verify an answer with Node's crypto.verify and nothing else
- [Source](https://github.com/PugarHuda/amanat): miner, scorer, contract, agent
- [What broke on the network](https://github.com/PugarHuda/amanat/blob/main/docs/bug-report.md): fourteen measured findings

## Data

Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0) for weather, marine and ensemble models and the reanalysis archive; GDACS for active tropical cyclones. Storm risk is derived from those readings and is ours.
